explanation: The theorem is about the library's own definitions `coordinateHalfSpace` (orthogonal complement of the span of a basis tail) and `bilateralShiftL` (the bilateral shift of a `HilbertBasis ℤ`), neither of which occurs in Mathlib (grep for `bilateralShift` / `coordinateHalfSpace` in Mathlib: no hits). The closest Mathlib statement is the general transport lemma `starProjection_map_apply` / `LinearIsometry.map_starProjection'` in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Basic.lean, which says `f (p.starProjection x) = (p.map f).starProjection (f x)` for a surjective (isometric) map. But deriving the target from it would require the library's own substantial result `map_coordinateHalfSpace` (that the shift carries the cut at `k` onto the cut at `k+1`) plus unfolding `bilateralShiftL` and `mul_apply_eq_comp`; that is more than one or two lines of routine glue, so it is not a special case. Hence no Mathlib duplicate was found.
